subject: Tide3B elevated error wave — mitigation timeline and canary rollout plan
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Patel <liam@stargazer.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Tide3B elevated error wave — mitigation timeline and canary rollout plan

Hi Liam —

We observed a sustained increase in 5xx and timeout responses originating from the Tide3B model serving pool that has been handling a portion of your production traffic since ~07:40 PT this morning. Early indicators:

- Error rate (5xx + timeouts) on Tide3B has risen from ~0.3% baseline to ~6.8% for the 07:40–08:05 window.
- Errors concentrated on longer prompt sequences (>1.5k tokens) and on the r2 inference nodes in us-west-2.
- Automated fallback routing to the quasar-lite variant protected ~40% of requests, but you likely saw increased latency/failures on some routes.

Immediate actions we've taken (already in flight):
1) Scaled additional us-west-2 inference nodes and moved older kernels to warm standby.
2) Deployed a targeted canary of an updated kernel/kv-cache handling patch to 5% of Tide3B capacity to validate fixes.
3) Enabled more aggressive prefix caching for long-sequence requests to reduce KV pressure.
4) Routed non-critical batch loads to dedicated burst capacity to free up steady nodes.

What to expect next (timeline):
- 09:00 PT: Canary verification (we'll monitor error rates and sample traces).
- 10:30 PT: If canary is stable, we will roll the fix to 50% capacity and continue monitoring.
- 13:00 PT: Full rollout target if metrics remain within normal thresholds.

We are attaching a small sample of error traces and ingestion metrics for your ops team to review. We will send a follow-up once the canary completes verification (or sooner if we see regression).

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the impact and will prioritize telemetry and rollback controls for any changes. If you'd like, we can stand up a quick bridge with your SREs; Connor can join.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tide3b_error_samples.txt (log snippets), ingest_metrics_0811-0911.csv (aggregated metrics)

From: Liam Patel <liam@stargazer.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tide3B elevated error wave — mitigation timeline and canary rollout plan

Thanks Michael — appreciate the quick heads up.

We routed ~70% of user traffic to an emergency fallback policy earlier, which reduced customer-facing errors, but our internal job queue still shows a backlog for longer-context requests (some timeouts are cascading). Two asks from our side:

1) Can you confirm whether any prompt-shaping or size-based throttles will be applied as part of the canary? We want to avoid unexpected truncation.
2) Please share a bridge link — we may want to shadow logs from our side.

Also: we saw ~10% higher error rate on a small subset of requests coming from us-east IPs; not sure if related.

— Liam
Ops Lead, Stargazer AI

Subject: Re: Tide3B elevated error wave — mitigation timeline and canary rollout plan

Michael / Olga —

Quick internal update for the bridge:

Observations so far:
- Root symptom looks like increased KV cache thrashing on r2 nodes when sequence length spikes coincide with concurrent checkpoints. This causes higher memory churn and intermittent GC pauses inside the runtime which surface as 504s/timeouts.
- The initial patch in the canary reduces aggressive KV segment eviction frequency and adds a lightweight lock around cache compaction paths. We saw a reduction in error rate from 7.1% -> 1.3% in the canary shard over a 20m window.

Planned steps (internal):
1) Continue canary observation for 90 minutes. If stable, promote to 50% and re-evaluate after another 60 minutes.
2) If we detect an increase in tail latency during promotion, automatic rollback to previous kernel will occur (we have fast rollback enabled).
3) Post-stabilization: compile a micro-optimization that changes KV prefetch threshold for long sequences (target 6–12h testing) and schedule for next maintenance window.

Action items for bridge: Connor will drive the rollout and provide minute-by-minute telemetry; Michael to coordinate external comms; Olga to collect heap profiles and enable expanded traces for the affected r2 nodes.

Connor O'Brien
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Tide3B — normalization and follow-up commitments (post-canary)

Liam —

Follow-up update: canary completed and verification criteria met. Summary of current state:

- Canary error rate stabilized at 0.9% (down from ~6.8% baseline spike).
- Roll to 50% occurred at ~11:35 PT with continued improvement; we reached 100% rollout at 13:05 PT after no regressions observed in secondary telemetry slices.
- We kept the quasar-lite fallback in place during the rollout; as of 15:20 PT, your customer-facing error rate is consistent with the pre-incident baseline (~0.4%).

Immediate commitments and next steps:
1) Root cause: an interaction between the KV cache compaction path and our older r2 kernel which increases GC pressure for long sequence workloads. The canary patch reduces eviction aggressiveness and serializes compaction to avoid pathological thrash.
2) Permanent fix timeline: we'll land and QA an optimized prefetch/threshold change and kernel tweak in a controlled release targeted for 2029-09-18 (7 days) with rollout gating.
3) Postmortem: we will publish a customer-facing postmortem that includes timelines, impact, and recommended request patterns to reduce exposure for long-context batches by 2029-09-14. Draft link: https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortem/tide3b-20290911 (internal view for now).
4) Compensatory measures: We are issuing a one-time service credit for incident impact (details to follow from billing) and will notify your account team.

Please let me know if you'd like a dedicated review session on the postmortem once the draft is published. Thanks again for the fast coordination on your side — that helped keep user-impact limited.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
